chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn al-Ash'ari, who said: He narrated to me Abu Abdullah al-Razi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
He said: I asked him about a man who willed a portion of his wealth, saying 'one-seventh of it.' (The Imam clarified the ruling regarding this specific phrasing).

key_terms.سَبْعُ ثُلُثِهِ: one-seventh of it (referring to the portion)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on a bequest phrased as 'one-seventh of my wealth' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal interpretation of a testator's bequest of 'one-seventh' of their wealth, addressing the ambiguity in fractional inheritance shares. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach to resolving discrepancies between literal phrasing and intended portions in wills, ensuring the distribution aligns with Islamic equity. The narration underscores the Imam's role in providing precise legal guidance for personal status matters.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-65 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Abu Abdullah al-Razi, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Khalid that he asked Abil Hassan (s), “How much of one’s wealth should be used, if one has willed that some of his wealth be spent in a certain way?”
